story_review.one_viewing_summary: A driverless white car picks up at a San Antonio airport curb with nobody at the wheel. A map shows the service began in a 60 square mile area in February. In April one empty car was carried off in Salado Creek and another sat stranded in floodwater. A federal recall record covers 3,791 units and says the software may let a car slow, then drive into standing water, which the film acts out. The remedy is stamped 'under development', interim weather limits and updates reached every car by April 20, and the close holds the open airport ride beside the unfinished remedy.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening asks what the federal record says now that anyone can hail a driverless ride to the airport. The ending answers with the same kind of curb and an open door beside the record card stamped 'Under development'. No remedy date or human outcome is invented, and every non-original example carries its own disclosure chip.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (12.8 to 13.2 s): the pale tabletop map cuts to an overhead creek with no carried visual element. The bridge relies on the new disclosure chip and the caption, which is honest but abrupt. The phone/arrival order at 1.4 to 6.2 s is the weakest causal moment within a scene.
